metadata.title: Cathie Wood Loaded Up On Anthropic’s Stock During IPO

content.text:
Closely followed investor Cathie Wood loaded up on Anthropic's (ANT) stock during the artificial intelligence (A.I.) company's market debut.
Wood's company, Ark Invest, added Anthropic shares across all of its major funds when the A.I. startup held its initial public offering (IPO) on Nov. 19.
Wood's firm bought $90.8 million U.S. worth of Anthropic stock across six of its investment funds, according to a statement from the company.

Anthropic's stock rose 17% in its first day of trading, closing at $97.17 U.S. per share, up from its IPO price of $83 U.S.
However, ANT stock was down 10% in premarket trading on Nov. 20 and changing hands at $87 U.S.
The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across Ark Invest's funds. In the $6.1 billion U.S. ARK Innovation ETF (BATS: $ARKK), Anthropic is currently a 0.3% stake.
That compares to a 21% stake for Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA) and SpaceX (NASDAQ: $SPCX), that fund's biggest holdings.
Wood is known for focusing her investments on stocks of companies that she feels are innovative or at the leading edge of technology, including A.I., electric vehicles and microchips.
The ARKK fund has declined 39% in the past five years to trade at $68.93 U.S. per share.
